newsitem.title: UK: CHINA SEEN IMPORTING SUGAR FROM WORLD MARKET IN 98.
newsitem.headline: CHINA SEEN IMPORTING SUGAR FROM WORLD MARKET IN 98.

text.p: China is likely to import sugar from the world market in 1998 as a result of an expected increase in consumption, Czarnikow Sugar said on Thursday.
In its first estimate of the world sugar balance for 1997/98, Czarnikow said Chinese consumption would rise by 150,000 tonnes raw value in 1998 to 8.65 million.
China was expected to see a slight retraction in beet sugar production from 1.54 million tonnes to 1.45 million, while cane sugar output would rise by 200,000 tonnes to 6.05 million tonnes.
"...Since the resulting deficit will not be met solely by deliveries from Cuba, it follows that imports will be needed from the world market," Czarnikow said.
China had been absorbing unquantified volumes of imported sugar over the past season, making it difficult to assess domestic availability, it added.
